cluster_stories.title: US Moves to Bar China’s DeepSeek From Federal Agency Systems
cluster_stories.summary: The Trump administration barred civilian US government agencies from using products or services from Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek, citing a potential threat to national security from the company’s operations in China.
cluster_stories.headline: US BANS DEEPSEEK FROM GOVERNMENT... National Security Threat

cluster_stories.title: AI Tool That Hacked Korean Banks Was Used in Japan, GMO Says
cluster_stories.summary: The hackers who recently infiltrated some of Japan’s biggest companies used an AI tool developed in China and linked to a rash of breaches at South Korean banks last month, according to a Tokyo-based internet security firm.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINESE AI TOOL USED IN JAPAN BANK HACKS LINKED TO KOREA BREACHES

The order covers third-party tools built on DeepSeek’s models, and cites the risk that sensitive data could be shared with the Chinese government. cluster_stories.title: Leaked Anthropic Draft AI Regulatory Bill Is Unacceptable and Troubling
cluster_stories.summary: There is a newly leaked bill that Anthropic is purportedly shopping around is (if you assume its bugs get fixed). It is similar to the FRONTIER Act, with stronger preemption of state laws, stronger transparency provisions and weaker enforcement provisions. Having slept on this, I find it unacceptable that Anthropic is actively shopping exactly the type of bill I have warned we will need to fight against during the lame duck session. They are trying to use this last time with a Republican Congress to pass preemption of exactly the important state laws, and get some transparency but not much enforcement in exchange. This reads as intentional, that Anthropic is more afraid that the government might enforce rules against Anthropic, than they are worried about the ability of the government to enforce rules against everyone. cluster_stories.headline: LEAKED ANTHROPIC AI BILL SPARKS BACKLASH

cluster_stories.title: OpenAI Arrest Raises AI Espionage Concerns
cluster_stories.summary: Morgan Meaker, a senior writer for Bloomberg Weekend, tells Bloomberg This Weekend about the arrest of an OpenAI engineer accused of planting a covert recording device in an executive conference room, a case highlighting growing concerns about protecting sensitive AI technology. Meaker also explains to hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini how AI training work is shifting toward highly skilled experts and why that evolution could eventually reshape the professions providing that expertise. (Source: Bloomberg)
cluster_stories.headline: OPENAI ENGINEER ARRESTED for Planting Spy Device in Exec Conference Room

cluster_stories.title: What are self-replicating ‘AI worms’, and why is Anthropic worried about them?
cluster_stories.summary: The tech company says successful AI worms need more capability on less powerful devices, but current trends make that feasible by the end of the yearWarnings about what artificial intelligence might do in the future – together with alarming reports of what it has gotten up to already – are being issued so quickly that even security experts have difficulty triaging what to worry about.Yet a report this week from Anthropic’s offensive research team grabbed attention by describing a new, practical threat, one devoid of human characteristics or apocalyptic musings. The red team, as such internal testers are called, said it created a malicious AI program that spread autonomously through internet-connected “smart” televisions and could do the same inside other ordinary devices. cluster_stories.headline: ANTHROPIC WARNS: Self-Replicating AI Worms Coming by Year's End
